detailed_findings.finding: The argument that x_r <= g is valid because all coordinates are positive, hence nonnegative, so each coordinate is bounded by the total sum g.
The case g = 0 is handled correctly: since m >= 2 there is at least one positive coordinate, forcing the sum to be at least 1 and contradicting the defining sum condition.

The defining semigroup-style inequalities on indices i,j are omitted from the argument, but this is not a semantic drift because finiteness follows from weaker conditions already included in membership.

reason: The proof correctly derives the coordinatewise bounds from the positivity and sum constraint in the definition of K_{m,g}, then uses these bounds to place K_{m,g} inside the finite box {1,...,g}^{m-1} when g >= 1, and separately proves K_{m,0} = ∅ using m >= 2. The extra defining inequalities for K_{m,g} are not used, but this is acceptable since they are unnecessary for finiteness. The proof matches the semantic sketch and supports the stated role in the assembly.
